site.title: Gionnio — Things I made for fun
site.description: Personal projects by Gionnio: small native apps for macOS and a web tool. Made for my Mac

hero.title:
From my Mac 
to yours.
hero.lede: Native Mac apps and project for my daily driver: video library, updates, backups, retrogame. Built for me, shared with everyone. Open source.

apps.name: Renamy
apps.description: Renames and organizes your personal video library using official TMDB metadata, anime included. Preview every change before it happens.

blocks.title: // why I made it
blocks.text: I used FileBot for years. When I went looking for a free, open-source alternative that fit the way I work, I couldn't find one. So I built my own, with speed and simplicity as the whole point.

items.title: Smart title detection
items.text: Finds the movie or show title in messy filenames by anchoring on the year, the season or the episode number, even when it is only in the folder name.

items.title: Official metadata
items.text: Titles, years and posters come from TMDB, so every file gets the same, correct name.

items.title: TV series
items.text: Understands `SxxExx`, `1x02`, absolute numbering and `Season 1` folders, and asks once for a whole series when a title is ambiguous.

items.title: Anime
items.text: Anime-style names are matched on AniList and converted to the TMDB title and numbering that Plex and Jellyfin read.

items.title: Plex, Jellyfin & Emby
items.text: Optional folder structure and ID tags in the formats media servers expect.

items.title: Fix any match
items.text: Search by title, TMDB ID or a themoviedb.org link when the guess is wrong.

items.title: Undo
items.text: Revert the last rename or move, including the folders it created.

notes.text: Start from a folder, or drop files in.
Pick the right title when there are several.

apps.name: Encody
apps.tagline: Power users still get the cockpit, just not by default.
apps.description: Re-encodes and remuxes your video library, keeping HDR10, HDR10+ and Dolby Vision intact. Drop, encode, done, or dive into every audio and subtitle track.

blocks.title: // why I made it
blocks.text: After years of HandBrake, I realized I only ever used three or four presets of my own, refined over time for exactly what I needed. So I wrote a small terminal tool that ran just those, and called it MediaEnc. That tool became the engine behind Encody.

items.title: Batch queue
items.text: Drop files or folders, reorder, enable or skip items, import and export the queue.

items.title: HDR aware
items.text: Detects HDR10, HDR10+, HLG and Dolby Vision and re-injects the dynamic metadata after encoding, even when cropping or downscaling.

items.title: Checked output
items.text: Every finished file is read back: a truncated encode never passes as done, and missing HDR metadata or tracks are flagged.

items.title: Presets you can trust
items.text: Custom presets are saved only after a real test encode passes.

items.title: Film grain detection
items.text: Measures grain on every file and suggests the right preset.

items.title: Benchmark & quality check
items.text: Compare presets on automatic samples and check results with VMAF, XPSNR, ColorVideoVDP or SSIM.

items.title: Track selection
items.text: Choose audio and subtitle tracks per file, with smart audio modes.

notes.text: Default settings for every imported files

apps.name: Tilefont
apps.tagline: Any font, eight pixels at a time.
apps.description: Turns TrueType and OpenType fonts into font images ready for GB Studio, accents included. Pick a font, check the preview, drop it into your project. Play!

blocks.title: // why I made it
blocks.text: As a lifelong retro gamer and Nintendo fan, I've been having a lot of fun with GB Studio. Good assets are hard to come by, though, and the most original ones are usually the ones you make yourself. Fonts are no exception, but drawing a font image by hand, letter by letter, felt clunky. Tilefont makes that part effortless.

items.title: GB Studio ready
items.text: 128×112 image with 8×8 tiles, the same colours and layout as GB Studio's own fonts.

items.title: Accents included
items.text: Extended characters 128–255 with a .json mapping, so à, é, € and friends just work.

items.title: Variable width
items.text: Magenta markers for proportional text, or 8 px fixed width.

items.title: Live preview
items.text: Check the grid and type a test sentence laid out the way GB Studio shows it.

items.title: Fit to tiles
items.text: Picks the largest size that fits and warns about clipped or missing characters.

items.title: Straight to your project
items.text: One click saves the font into the assets/fonts folder of your GB Studio project.

apps.name: PS2 Manager
apps.description: Organizes backups of the PS2 and PS1 games you own for Open PS2 Loader. Cover art, game IDs and file names, all sorted out for you.

blocks.title: // why I made it
blocks.text: I'm a huge retrogamer. After too many late nights with outdated tools and wrong guides, I finally figured out how OPL actually expects things to be laid out. I wrote a few terminal scripts to prepare the hard drive or MX4SIO for my Free McBoot PS2, so I could play without putting my physical collection at risk. The GUI was the natural next step.

items.title: Drag & drop install
items.text: Drop PS2 `.iso` backups to copy them, PS1 `.cue`/`.bin` backups to convert them to `.VCD`.

items.title: PS1 via POPStarter
items.text: Creates the launcher for each game with your own imported files and copies the right patches.

items.title: Multi-disc games
items.text: Groups discs, writes the files OPL needs and renames everything to a standard format.

items.title: Titles & covers
items.text: Game names read from the disc image, covers downloaded one by one or for the whole library.

items.title: Per-game settings
items.text: Compatibility modes, virtual memory cards and cheats for every game.

items.title: Tools
items.text: Rename, export, convert back to BIN/CUE, defragment and delete, with a queue and progress.

apps.name: Upgrady
apps.description: Checks every app on your Mac for updates, Sparkle, Homebrew casks and App Store apps included, and installs them for you.

blocks.title: // why I made it
blocks.text: MacUpdater started giving me trouble on macOS 27, and none of the alternatives handled Homebrew the way I wanted. So I built my own: exactly what I needed, nothing more.

items.title: Menu bar app
items.text: Lives in the menu bar with the number of available updates: update one app or all of them in one click, with progress.

items.title: Sparkle, Homebrew & App Store
items.text: Sparkle apps are updated with their own feed and signature, casks through `brew`, App Store apps (iPhone and iPad ones too) are checked.

items.title: Third-party taps
items.text: Reads every installed tap, including personal ones like `gionnio/tap`.

items.title: Release notes
items.text: Shows the release notes of every version you are skipping.

items.title: Adopt manual installs
items.text: Links apps installed by hand to their Homebrew cask.

items.title: Always current
items.text: Checks in the background, notifies you, and refreshes by itself when apps are installed or removed.

apps.name: Tazzina
apps.tagline: The world needed one more caffeine app. Probably.
apps.description: A menu bar app with timed sessions, automatic triggers, sounds, and closed-lid mode. Brewed in Italy.

blocks.title: // why I made it
blocks.text: I wanted something like Amphetamine, but simpler, lighter, and open source. There were already a thousand of them. This is number 1,001.

items.title: One click
items.text: Left click on the cup turns it on or off, right click opens the menu.

items.title: Sessions
items.text: Indefinitely, for a while, until a time, or as long as an app is running.

items.title: Triggers
items.text: Stays awake on its own when your rules match: apps, Wi-Fi, displays, power, battery, time, devices.

items.title: Closed lid
items.text: Keeps a MacBook running with the lid closed, and always restores normal sleep afterwards.

items.title: Safety
items.text: Ends the session when the battery is low or the charger is unplugged.

items.title: Automation
items.text: `tazzina://` links for Terminal and Shortcuts.

apps.name: Tiny Little Patcher
apps.tagline: ROM Patcher straight to your browser.
apps.description: Applies IPS, UPS and BPS patches to your ROMs, checking every checksum and fixing SNES headers for you. Nothing to install.

apps.name: DumpBoy
apps.tagline: Childhood memories, safe on your Mac.
apps.description: A native app for the GBFlash and Submodule GB01 readers: back up the Game Boy, Game Boy Color and Game Boy Advance cartridges you own, save and restore game saves with verification at every step, browse Game Boy Camera photos and play right away.

blocks.title: // why I made it
blocks.text: Who hasn’t picked up a Game Boy cartridge, eager to revisit an old save file filled with memories and joy, only to discover that, over the years, the battery has died and the save file is gone? I wasn’t satisfied with the software for the most common flashers on the market for macOS, so I created this tool, which has the features I was looking for. My old games, now always with me.

apps.name: Posta
apps.description: A native Liquid Glass Gmail client: Apple Mail's feel with Gmail's labels, search and conversations.

blocks.title: // why I made it
blocks.text: Come on, who doesn't want their Gmail account in Apple Mail, without all the usual limitations?

items.title: Mail-style layout
items.text: Mailboxes and nested labels, conversation list and full threads, like Apple Mail.

items.title: Real Gmail
items.text: Labels, threads, archive, stars and Gmail search syntax through the Gmail API.

items.title: Liquid Glass
items.text: A native toolbar with grouped actions that feels at home on macOS.

items.title: Notifications
items.text: Reply, archive or delete straight from the notification.

items.title: Always there
items.text: Keeps syncing from the menu bar when the window is closed.

items.title: Keyboard first
items.text: Mail shortcuts plus optional Gmail single-key shortcuts.

apps.name: Taccuino
apps.description: A fast, native text and code editor with tabs, sessions that keep your unsaved drafts, syntax colors, regex search and macros.

blocks.title: // why I made it
blocks.text: On Windows I lived in Notepad++: open it, paste something, close it, and find everything still there the next day. I wanted that same habit on my Mac, in an app that looks like it belongs there.

items.title: Never asks to save
items.text: Quit whenever you want: open files and unsaved drafts, even untitled ones, come back as you left them.

items.title: 40 languages
items.text: Syntax colors, seven themes and an outline of functions, classes and headings.

items.title: Find everywhere
items.text: Normal, extended and regex search in the document, in every open tab or in a whole folder.

items.title: Encodings
items.text: Detects 22 encodings and any line ending, and converts between them.

items.title: Line tools
items.text: Sort, deduplicate, trim, join, move, duplicate, comment and change case from one menu.

items.title: Macros
items.text: Record what you type and the commands you use, then replay it once or a thousand times.

apps.name: Platea Home
apps.description: A tvOS-style home screen for Android TV, Google TV and Fire TV: six apps in a dock, no ads, no sponsored rows, no internet access. Around 100 KB.
apps.note: Early release: tested on Sony BRAVIA, TCL and Fire TV Stick 4K Max.

blocks.title: // why I made it
blocks.text: My TVs opened on rows of ads and things I never asked for. I wanted the calm of an Apple TV home screen, so I tried theming other launchers first. None of them came close, so I made my own: small, offline, and quiet.

items.title: A real top shelf
items.text: The focused app's category, name and one line about it, big and readable from the couch.

items.title: Six apps in the dock
items.text: Hold OK to move, add, replace, hide an app or open its info. One dimmed row below, then All apps.

items.title: Quick settings
items.text: Picture, sound, network, inputs and the volume bar in a side panel, without leaving Home.

items.title: Inputs that know their devices
items.text: Live TV and the HDMI ports, with the device names read over HDMI-CEC.

items.title: Three palettes
items.text: Graphite, Night blue or Day, with reduced animations if you want them.

items.title: Sipario
items.text: A quiet screen saver: the time, a line and the date on black, moving a little every minute.

items.title: Offline and light
items.text: No `INTERNET` permission, no libraries, no tracking. About 100 KB, around 35 MB of RAM.

items.title: Fire TV too
items.text: Fire OS keeps Amazon's home, so on a Fire TV it opens through dumbtv's Home guard. Debloating is left to CleanYourTV and dumbtv, model by model.

blocks.title: How it works
blocks.caption: Fire TV Stick 4K Max, Day palette. The interface follows the TV's language.

notes.text: The top shelf names the focused app.
Six apps in the dock: focus lifts the tile.
Every other app, one click away.

blocks.caption: Hold OK on an app: Move, Remove from dock, Hide, App info.
Move: Left and Right to slide it, OK to drop it, Back to cancel.
Quick settings, with the volume bar.
Inputs, with device names over HDMI-CEC (Sony BRAVIA, Graphite palette).
Launcher settings: three palettes, previewed before you pick one.
All apps, six per row. Dock apps have a dot.

blocks.title: Get it
blocks.text: Platea Home is installed over the network with `adb`: download `platea-home.apk` from the releases and follow the README, or open the repo in an AI coding agent and paste `PROMPT.md`. Undo is one command.

apps.name: Platea
apps.tagline: Every film the way it was made.
apps.description: A Jellyfin client for Android TV, Google TV and Fire TV, made for a curated 4K library: direct play first, real Dolby Vision, HDR10+, audio passthrough and subtitles done right.
apps.note: First public release: tested on Fire TV Stick 4K Max and Sony BRAVIA, with Jellyfin 12.

blocks.title: // why I made it
blocks.text: I prepare every film in my library with care, then the TV client remuxed it, dropped the Dolby Vision or stuttered on 24p. I started from Wholphin to fix the playback engine and ended up with a client of my own: one that sends the file as it is and shows exactly how it was served.

items.title: Direct play first
items.text: The device profile comes from what the TV really decodes and shows, so the server sends the file as it is. Conversion is a logged fallback you can switch off.

items.title: Real Dolby Vision
items.text: Dolby Vision, HDR10+ and HDR10 on the right decoder, with a notice when a file loses Dolby Vision.

items.title: Sound as recorded
items.text: Passthrough for Dolby Digital Plus and Atmos; TrueHD and DTS decoded by the app when the TV cannot take them.

items.title: Smooth 24p
items.text: Refresh rate switching before playback, and tunneled playback on TVs that only offer 60 Hz.

items.title: Subtitles done right
items.text: PGS and ASS drawn by the app, forced-only by default, full subtitles when the audio is in another language.

items.title: Straight from the NAS
items.text: Optional: in direct play the file is read from the SMB share, like Infuse, with the server stream as a fallback.

items.title: Its own interface
items.text: Velvet and gold: featured home, libraries, technical sheet, collections, people, voice search, seek bar previews, skip intro, profiles with PIN.

items.title: Updates itself
items.text: New releases are offered on the home and installed over the app. No analytics, no telemetry.

blocks.title: How it works
blocks.caption: Fire TV Stick 4K Max, movie page (Italian interface). The technical sheet says how the file will be served before you press Play.

notes.text: Direct play with Dolby Vision: no remux, no conversion.
Video, HDR, audio, subtitles and file, read from the server.
Audio and subtitles, remembered per title and per series.
Cast: every person opens their titles in your library.

blocks.caption: Home: a featured title, then Continue watching and the latest additions.
Library: filters, genres and sorting, watched titles marked.
Series page: seasons, episodes, the theme song from Jellyfin.

blocks.title: Get it
blocks.text: Download the APK from the releases (`arm64-v8a` for most TVs, `armeabi-v7a` for the Fire TV Stick) and install it with Downloader or `adb`, as the README explains. From then on Platea updates itself. It is free software under the GPL-2.0, a fork of Wholphin by damontecres.
